email.subject: Re: Reaction delivery bundling, from today
email.body:
You said today, in the delivery routing ruling: "we route every reaction through one bundle per run per person, not one message per skill — a person should get one thing to read, not four." The same memo has Tina pushing back on the batching window, and you held: "the bundle closes when the run closes, and a skill that misses the close waits for the next run rather than sending on its own." The memo also records the rejected alternative, per-skill delivery with client-side collapsing, which "moves the ordering problem onto the reader."

So now a person gets one bundle per run, and that bundle closes with the run. A skill that misses the close waits for the next run instead of sending its own message. Per-skill delivery is set aside. Tina's objection to the batching window is still in the memo, and nothing in it has been answered yet.

My read is that anyone who expected separate sends from each skill should now expect one bundle, and that anything built around per-skill messages no longer has to be built. That suggests to me that a skill which misses the close will look late to the reader. If that holds, the ordering work stays with us and not with the person reading.

Does that hold for the batching window Tina raised, or is her concern still open? How long can a skill wait for the next run before anyone notices the gap?
